doc: plan/BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md §1, §3, §4, §5, §6, §9 — one entry per regime, plus the vocabularies every row is addressed by. §9 retires three namings: P1/P2/P3 (they encoded eval scope, which is now one thing for every regime), Dataset 2 / Dataset 3 (they conflated the corpus with the pipeline that produced the truth), and the board ids `main`/`dev`/`entrants` (`main` and `dev` are now the two regime ids; `entrants` is no longer a board at all — it is the anchor block). A board whose `frozen` hashes are still TODO refuses every `add`. Both live regimes and the anchor block were frozen on 2026-09-02 — the store manifest re-read on Fir after t78's DNase p-value rebuild, the regime jsons as t79 rewrote them and this repo tracks them — so a row scored against that pair now lands and a row scored against anything else still cannot. `pending` lists methods whose results are still computing; `build` drops an entry once a row for that method is stamped.

address.rule: §1 — every cell on the board is addressed by these six. If any field is unknown for a row, the row does not go in the ranked table. `add` refuses such a row and the compiler has no place to put one.
address.eli5: A number on this page is never just a score. It is a score for one method, trained under one regime, measured against one truth, on one panel of experiments, over one set of chromosomes, with one metric. Change any of the six and it is a different number.

store.label: store (ENCODE4 2020)
store.eli5: The truth track as ENCODE4 pipeline v1.5.1 produced it in Aug–Sep 2020, ingested into CANDI_STORE. Counts, −log10 p and peak calls all exist here, so all three arms score.

challenge.label: challenge (2019)
challenge.eli5: The same ENCODE experiments, bridged 1:1 on accession, but as the 2019 challenge organizers processed them. Only the pipeline differs. If a method's standing holds under both truths, its result is not an artifact of the pipeline that made our truth.
challenge.greyed_arms_note: §7 — the 2019 data has no counts and no peak calls, so the count and peak arms are greyed out under this truth. Scoring peaks against store truth while the p-value arm used challenge truth would put two truths in one row.
challenge.scorer_note: §6 — one scorer, one grid, both truths. The Synapse bigwigs load into candi.bench.external on the store's grid, with the store's blacklist policy and the same assay panel on both sides. This view no longer reproduces the published 2019 numbers exactly, and that is accepted.

V_breadth.label: V_ breadth
V_breadth.subtitle: 45 experiments, 22 assays
V_breadth.eli5: The whole validation panel. Every trainable method selected its best checkpoint here, by the same rule, so this column is optimistic by construction — identically for everyone. That is why B_ exists.

V_matched.label: V_ matched
V_matched.subtitle: the 8 assays B_ contains
V_matched.eli5: The same validation predictions, aggregated over only the assays the test panel has. It is never ranked. It exists so the V_→B_ step is readable: without it a reader attributes the whole drop to the model, when most of it is the exam changing.

B_.label: B_ test
B_.subtitle: 51 experiments, 8 assays
B_.eli5: The test panel. Never read during training. Predicted exactly once, from the single checkpoint the method selected on V_. Re-scoring those stored predictions is free; re-predicting is not.

panel_rules.rendering: §5 — V_ and B_ render side by side inside one regime, never as two views of one thing.
panel_rules.subtraction: §5.3 — never subtract V_ breadth from B_. V_ matched is the only legal subtraction, and it prints the panel caveat with it.

held-out.label: held-out
held-out.subtitle: chr20 + chr21 + chr22
held-out.eli5: 6,478,903 bins, 5.34 % of the store, split 40 / 29 / 31 % so no single chromosome owns the macro average. No method's transferable parameters were fit here, so nothing can be memorised. This is the ranked number.

genome-wide.label: genome-wide
genome-wide.subtitle: all 23 chromosomes
genome-wide.eli5: The same prediction pass, aggregated over all 121,241,684 bins. It is for methodological comparability with a literature that scores this way — it is never ranked.
genome-wide.blanking_rule: §4 — printed only where the method is out-of-sample somewhere. For a method whose transferable parameters were fit at every position (Avocado, ChromImpute, Lavawizard, in both regimes) the number is a memorisation score, not an imputation score, and the in-sample-fraction badge is not a strong enough warning to carry it. Those cells are blank, and a blanked cell is not computed — it does not exist.

edice-embedding-substitution.label: embedding substitution
edice-embedding-substitution.eli5: §7 — eDICE queries a V_ or B_ target using that target's paired T_ cell's learned embedding. Rule 1 permits it: a regime is a data contract, not a parameter contract, and the scored track is still never read. But it is a different kind of access than the other methods get, so the row carries this marker. Comparable, and disclosed.

no-selection.label: no selection
no-selection.applies_to: methods with no checkpoint to pick
no-selection.eli5: §5 — this method trains once and produces one model. There is no checkpoint to pick and no knob tuned on V_. It keeps its V_ score, which is a same-panel comparison and worth having. The marker is not cosmetic: V_ gave this method none of the optimistic lift every trainable method got, so its V_→B_ behaviour is not comparable to CANDI's without accounting for that.

selection-key-pval-mse.label: selected on pval mse
selection-key-pval-mse.eli5: selects its checkpoint on pval mse, not count-arm CRPS; a deliberate asymmetry that handicaps CANDI — PI ruling 2026-09-01
selection-key-pval-mse.detail: §5 and the 2026-09-01 ruling — the uniform selection rule binds the panel, the instrument, the scope and the cadence, but NOT the key. §7 gives no rival a count head, and the pval CRPS needs a σ-table Rule 1 forbids fitting on V_. So CANDI selects on count-arm CRPS and these three select on pval mse. Which way it cuts, stated so nobody has to re-derive it: CANDI is tuned on an arm no rival can enter while the head-to-head is the pval arm, so CANDI is selected on a different objective from the one it is compared on and the rivals are not. That handicaps CANDI.

eic.19.label: eic.19→20,21,22
eic.19.subtitle: trained on chr19
eic.19.rows_note: CANDI, the four retrained rivals, and the five naive baselines. One CANDI row — the current best; version history is a separate figure, never extra rows.
eic.19.eli5: The primary regime. Every method's transferable parameters are fit on chromosome 19 and nothing else, then every method is scored on chromosomes 20, 21 and 22. Per-position adaptation on the eval chromosomes counts as inference, not training, and is open to every method.
eic.19.train_scope: chr19 — 2,344,704 training bins, 1.93 % of the store

eval_set.pairs: declared eval_pairs of the EIC corpus — 26 T_→V_ cell pairs and 12 T_→B_ cell pairs

frozen.frozen_note: Frozen 2026-09-02, when the first rows were stamped. `store_manifest_hash` is `sha256sum /project/def-maxwl/mforooz/CANDI_STORE/eic/manifest.json` read on Fir at that moment; that file's mtime is 2026-08-30 22:22 PDT, so it predates every scoring pass on this board and no pass read a different build of it. `regime_sha256` is `sha256sum configs/regime.eic_19.json` as this repo tracks it. A real pass never reads the shipped regime — `tools/declare_eval_pairs.py split` cuts it to one panel first — so the row gate accepts the shipped name or the derived single-panel sibling of the row's own panel.

noise_floor.note: §15 — the resolution limit on these panels is not measured yet (t86: two seeds of one method, same data, on the V_ breadth panel and on the 8-assay panels separately, because they do not have the same resolution). Nothing is ranked until it lands; rows go up unranked before then. AGENTS.md §7.2 records that a seed change alone moves pooled CRPS by 0.1195, so this is not a formality.

caveats: Every row that used to be on this page is void (§3.3): the old board scored all 23 chromosomes, chr19 included, and chr19 is the chromosome CANDI trained on. Those numbers are not carried forward, and no new row has been scored yet.

Under this regime CANDI is in-sample on 1 of 23 chromosomes. That fraction is part of the number's address, and the page prints it beside any row whose score json carries a per-cell fraction. No producer writes one yet, so no row shows a figure — an absent fraction is drawn as nothing rather than as zero.

The board measures missing-mark transfer within a seen cell type (§8). Every eval pair is a mark the V_ or B_ cell has and its paired T_ cell lacks, so the model always sees other tracks from the same cell type. CANDI's zero-shot claim is not tested here.

Nothing on this board is ranked yet, and no gap between two rows is readable yet. §15's resolution limit (t86) is not measured, and AGENTS.md §7.2 records that a seed change alone moves pooled CRPS by 0.1195 while the target-clustered noise floor on macro CRPS is ~0.09. Until t86 lands, read a row as a number that exists, never as a number that beats another.

ChromImpute's B_ rows are point-only on 3 of their 51 tracks. Its σ table was fitted on a 6-cell training draw that carries no ATAC-seq, so the three ATAC-seq B_ experiments (T_DND-41, T_NCI-H929, T_RWPE2) got no spread and every σ-derived key on them was withheld: the distributional metrics on those rows are aggregated over 48 tracks, the point metrics over 51. Named in each json as `provenance.point_only_tracks`; recorded in cruxvault/results/t81/PRED_B_CI.md. Widening the σ draw would break the uniform 12-cell draw, so the gap is disclosed rather than closed.

Lavawizard's B_ rows carry the same point-only gap on the same 3 of their 51 tracks: its σ table was fitted on a 12-cell training draw in which ATAC-seq is not a training assay, so the three ATAC-seq B_ experiments (T_DND-41, T_NCI-H929, T_RWPE2) got no spread and the distributional metrics on those rows are aggregated over 48 tracks against 51 for the point metrics (`provenance.point_only_tracks`; cruxvault/results/t81/W3_LAVA_19.md §R.2, §R.6). That σ table has a second, separate gap: 2 rare-mark self-pair tracks were skipped in the fit, so H2AK9ac and H4K12ac have no σ row at all. Neither mark is in this regime's V_ or B_ panel, so every row stamped here is unaffected by that second gap; a later panel carrying either would be point-only for it.

knn1's rows carry no distributional cell on the pval arm at all, on the V_ panel under store truth and on the B_ panel under challenge truth alike. The pass ran with no σ table, so `provenance.sigma_source` reads `none` on all 45 tracks and the scorer withheld every σ-derived key: `pval/crps`, `pval/pit_ks`, `pval/coverage_95` and `pval/gaussian_nll` are ABSENT from the row rather than zero, and its badge is the third σ state, `point-only — no spread`. Its point metrics stand over the same 45 experiments and 22 assays as every other V_breadth row here, so those columns are directly comparable and only the distributional ones are blank. knn1 was the first row on this board to carry a count arm, and it no longer stands alone: knn5's, avg's and marginal's V_breadth rows carry one too, and CANDI's own two stamped 2026-09-04 carry one over the same 45 experiments and 22 assays, so the count sub-board at store.V_breadth holds five methods on both scopes. Nothing on it is ranked either, so no placement there is a comparison. Read from the row's own `missing_metrics` and `provenance.sigma_source`; cited to cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_EIC19.md. The same absence is on knn1's challenge-truth B_ row stamped 2026-09-02: `provenance.sigma_source` reads `none` on all 51 of its tracks, the same four keys are in its `missing_metrics`, and its point metrics stand over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays as every other row at that address (cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_B.md). The same four keys are ABSENT from its store-truth B_ and V_matched rows stamped 2026-09-03, for the same reason: `provenance.sigma_source` reads `none` on all 51 tracks of the B_ json and all 45 of the V_ json, and each row records the four in its `missing_metrics`. On both of those addresses knn1 is so far the only method carrying a count arm at all — every other row at store.B_ and at store.V_matched reads 0 experiments on the count arm — while its point columns stand over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays (B_) and 21 and 7 (V_matched) as every other row at each address, so only the distributional pval cells are blank.

avg-arcsinh's σ table skips 2 of its 98 training self-pair tracks and so holds 29 assays: neither `H2AK9ac` nor `H4K12ac` has a σ row, the same rare-mark gap Lavawizard's tables carry. Its V_ rows are unaffected by that rare-mark gap — `provenance.sigma_source` reads `sigma_table` on all 45 of the scored V_ tracks, so every scored V_ experiment got a spread. Its B_ rows carry a different gap of the same kind: ATAC-seq has no row in that 29-assay table either, so the three ATAC-seq B_ experiments (T_DND-41, T_NCI-H929, T_RWPE2) read `sigma_source` `none` and every σ-derived key on them was withheld — the distributional metrics on avg-arcsinh's B_ rows are aggregated over 48 tracks against 51 for the point metrics, the same 48+3 split ChromImpute's and Lavawizard's B_ rows carry (`provenance.point_only_tracks`; cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_B.md). Read from the table's own `skipped_tracks` and `n_tracks` at /project/def-maxwl/mforooz/t81_sigma/avg-arcsinh/sigma_eic_19.json; its `fitted_on` is "training-residuals: sigma.eic_19.json T_ self-pairs, 12 cells, chroms ['chr19']", which the row copies verbatim into its badge. Avocado's B_ rows carry the same 48+3 split for a third variant of the same cause, and the contrast with the Avocado caveat below is the point: Avocado's σ table skips no track and holds 31 assays over 98 tracks, but ATAC-seq is not one of those 31, so the three ATAC-seq B_ experiments (T_DND-41, T_NCI-H929, T_RWPE2) read `sigma_source` `none` and every σ-derived key on them was withheld — the distributional metrics on Avocado's store-truth and challenge-truth B_ rows are aggregated over 48 tracks against 51 for the point metrics. Its V_ rows are unaffected: `provenance.sigma_source` reads `sigma_table` on all 45 scored V_ tracks and `provenance.point_only_tracks` is empty there, so the split reaches its B_ cells and neither its V_breadth nor its V_matched cell (`provenance.point_only_tracks` in each B_ json, and the table at /project/def-maxwl/mforooz/t81_sigma/Avocado/sigma_eic_19.json; cruxvault/results/t81/W3_AVOCADO.md). eDICE's B_ rows stamped 2026-09-03 carry the same 48+3 split for a fourth variant of the same cause: its σ table skips no track and holds 31 assays over 98 tracks, but ATAC-seq is not one of those 31, so the three ATAC-seq B_ experiments (T_DND-41, T_NCI-H929, T_RWPE2) read `sigma_source` `none` and every σ-derived key on them was withheld — the distributional metrics on all three of eDICE's B_ rows — its two store-truth rows and the challenge-truth row stamped later the same day — are aggregated over 48 tracks against 51 for the point metrics. The challenge-truth B_ json names the same three ATAC-seq experiments in its own `point_only_tracks` and reads `sigma_source` `none` on the same 3 of its 51 tracks, so the split is measured again under the second truth rather than carried over from the first. Its V_ rows are unaffected: `provenance.sigma_source` reads `sigma_table` on all 45 scored V_ tracks and `provenance.point_only_tracks` is empty there, so neither its V_breadth nor its V_matched cell carries the split. Read from `provenance.point_only_tracks` in the B_ json and the table at /project/def-maxwl/mforooz/t81_sigma/eDICE/sigma_eic_19.json; cruxvault/results/t81/PRED_B_EDICE.md §2.

The genome-wide column is not the same field as the held-out one, and never will be. §4 blanks it for Avocado, ChromImpute and Lavawizard — their transferable parameters were fit at every position, so a genome-wide number there would be a memorisation score and a blanked cell is not computed — while eDICE, CANDI and the naive baselines do have one, and those are the rows stamped in it. CANDI is position-generalizing — it pins no parameter to a genomic position — so a genome-wide cell is legitimate for it, and its store-truth V_breadth row stamped 2026-09-04 is the first one it has. So a reader looking down the genome-wide column is looking at a subset of the methods on this page, chosen by §4 and not by what finished computing. No genome-wide cell is ranked under any circumstances.

marginal's rows carry no `pval/gwcorr` and no `pval/gwspear`, on the B_ panel under challenge truth and on the V_breadth panel under store truth alike. The baseline predicts one constant value per track, so its prediction has zero variance and its Pearson and Spearman correlation against the truth is undefined — not a number, per track, by construction: a property of the baseline and not a failed pass. Under this board's rule an undefined metric on a baseline is DROPPED with this caveat, never silently and never as 0: the scorer wrote neither key into `macro.pval` nor into `panels.pval.B`, the row records both in `missing_metrics`, and the two correlation columns are blank for marginal alone. Every other key on the challenge-truth B_ row is a real number over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays as the rest of that address, the distributional ones included: the constant track still carries its own per-bin `signal_sigma`, so the row's σ badge is `native heteroscedastic` and its crps, pit_ks, coverage_95 and gaussian_nll are computed rather than withheld. Read from the score json's own `macro.pval` key set and the row's `missing_metrics`; cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_B.md. The same two keys are ABSENT for the same reason from marginal's store-truth V_breadth rows on this board stamped 2026-09-04, held-out and genome-wide each: the scorer wrote neither into `macro.pval` nor into the `genome_wide` block's own `macro.pval`, each row records both in `missing_metrics` and that is the whole of each list, and each was stamped with --allow-missing only after the gate refused it by name — naming those two keys and no others. Their remaining columns stand over the same 45 experiments and 22 assays as every other V_breadth row at each of those addresses, so only the two correlation cells are blank, and the count arm is full at 45 experiments on 22 assays, so marginal is on the count sub-board there. The scoring pass's own `.err` records the drop as warnings rather than silently: numpy's `invalid value encountered in divide` on the Pearson path and `ConstantInputWarning: An input array is constant; the correlation coefficient is not defined.` raised at src/candi/bench/eic.py:68 on the Spearman path, in slurm-logs/t49_score_57816340_4.err on Fir, and the job exited 0. Read from the score json's own `macro.pval` and `genome_wide.macro.pval` key sets and each row's `missing_metrics`; cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_EIC19.md.

avg-arcsinh carries no count arm on any row on this board. The baseline takes the pval mean in arcsinh space and sinh's it back, so it predicts in -log10 p only: the scorer wrote `macro.count` empty and every `panels[count]` block at 0 experiments and 0 assays, and the four count-arm registry metrics — `count/crps`, `count/crps_oracle_scaled`, `count/nb_nll` and `count/scale_error` — are ABSENT from its V_breadth, V_matched and B_ rows rather than zero. Each of those rows records all four in `missing_metrics`, and that is the whole of the list: no pval key is missing on any of them. So avg-arcsinh never appears on the count sub-board here, while its pval columns stand over the same experiments and assays as every other row at the same address and are directly comparable there. This is a property of the baseline, not a failed pass, and it is why each of those rows was stamped with --allow-missing only after the gate refused it without. Read from each row's own `missing_metrics` and the score json's own `macro` key set; cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_B.md.

Avocado carries no count arm on any row on this board. §7 gives no rival a count head, and Avocado predicts in -log10 p only: the scorer wrote `macro.count` empty and every `panels[count]` block at 0 experiments and 0 assays, so the four count-arm registry metrics — `count/crps`, `count/crps_oracle_scaled`, `count/nb_nll` and `count/scale_error` — are ABSENT from its V_breadth row rather than zero. The row records all four in `missing_metrics`, and that is the whole of the list: no pval key is missing. Its pval columns stand over the same 45 experiments and 22 assays as every other V_breadth row at this address and are directly comparable there. This is a property of the method, not a failed pass, and it is why the row was stamped with --allow-missing only after the gate refused it without. The same four keys are absent for the same reason from ChromImpute's, eDICE's and Lavawizard's V_breadth rows here, so the count sub-board at store.V_breadth carries no rival at all and the five methods on it are the four baselines and CANDI itself, whose store-truth V_breadth rows stamped 2026-09-04 carry a count arm over 45 experiments and 22 assays. Avocado's σ table skips no track — 98 tracks over 31 assays, `skipped_tracks` empty — so the rare-mark gap recorded above for Lavawizard's and avg-arcsinh's tables does not reach it, and H2AK9ac and H4K12ac each have a σ row. Read from the row's own `missing_metrics`, the score json's own `macro` key set and the table at /project/def-maxwl/mforooz/t81_sigma/Avocado/sigma_eic_19.json; cruxvault/results/t81/W3_AVOCADO.md. The same four keys are ABSENT for the same reason from its store-truth B_ and V_matched rows stamped 2026-09-03, and each of those two was likewise stamped with --allow-missing only after the gate refused it by name; their pval columns stand over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays (B_) and the same 21 and 7 (V_matched) as every other row at each of those addresses. Its challenge-truth B_ row records the same four for a different reason — under challenge truth the count arm is absent by rule for every method, which is also why that row alone adds pval/auprc and pval/peak_base_rate — and it needed no --allow-missing at all, so Avocado appears on no count sub-board on this board under either truth. The claim above that its σ table skips no track is about the rare marks only and is not a claim that its rows carry no σ gap: the point-only caveat above records the 48-of-51 ATAC-seq gap on its B_ rows. The same four count keys are ABSENT for the same reason from eDICE's store-truth B_ and V_matched rows stamped 2026-09-03, held-out and genome-wide each: §7 gives eDICE no count head either, so its scorer wrote `macro.count` empty and every `panels[count]` block at 0 experiments and 0 assays, each of the four rows records the four keys in `missing_metrics` and that is the whole of each list, and each was stamped with --allow-missing only after the gate refused it by name. Their pval columns stand over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays (B_) and the same 21 and 7 (V_matched) as every other row at each of those addresses, so the count sub-boards at store.B_ and store.V_matched still hold knn1 alone. eDICE's challenge-truth B_ row stamped 2026-09-03 records the same four for a different reason — under challenge truth the count arm is absent by rule for every method, which is also why that row alone adds pval/auprc and pval/peak_base_rate — and it needed no --allow-missing at all, so eDICE appears on no count sub-board on this board under either truth.

Avocado's V_ rows and its B_ rows on this board are not the same numerical path. Its V_ predictions were made on a 1g.10gb MIG slice with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) live, while its B_ predictions were made on CPU nodes in fp32 — predict.py:71 resolves the device to cpu when the allocation carries no GPU, and predict.py:133 enables autocast only when device.type == "cuda", so it disabled itself — because the GPU queue gave the once-only B_ arrays no projected start at all on 2026-09-03 and the pass was re-priced onto the CPU partitions. Nothing else differs: the same checkpoints, the same σ table, the same sinh-and-clip inversion and the same declared panel, so the V_ to B_ step for Avocado alone carries a precision term no other method's carries, and how large that term is was not measured — a CPU V_ re-run to measure it was not run (cruxvault/results/t81/W3_AVOCADO.md §26).

CANDI's rows on this board were predicted on CPU nodes, not on a GPU, and the PI ruled on 2026-09-04 that those CPU roots ARE the canonical CANDI prediction roots. The V_ panel came from the 23-task chromosome-sharded array 57953578 (one chromosome per task, --gres=none --cpus-per-task=8 --mem=16G, all 23 COMPLETED 0:0) writing /scratch/mforooz/t81_pred/CANDI/eic_19/V_cpu, and that root is the ONLY CANDI V_ prediction root there is: no V_ directory exists beside it, the name V_cpu records the DEVICE the pass ran on and not a sibling status, and the GPU submission that would have written a V_ folder, 57944437, has never started — queued 2026-09-03T02:19, still PENDING (Priority) when these rows were stamped, and it has written nothing. The B_ panel is the canonical /project/def-maxwl/mforooz/t81_pred_B/CANDI/eic_19/B_, written by the 23-task array 57953581 of the same shape and merged into that single root. Both passes were re-priced onto the CPU partitions because the GPU queue gave the once-only CANDI predict jobs no projected start from 2026-09-02 19:25 onward. On the B_ array alone, task 0 (chr1) was killed OUT_OF_MEMORY against the 16 G ceiling — MaxRSS is linear in chromosome length across its siblings and chr1 extrapolates to ~18 GiB — so chr1 alone was re-predicted unsharded at 32 G over the same root and merged with the other 22; the V_ array took no such kill and all 23 of its shards completed at 16 G. So a reader comparing a B_ cell here against a V_ cell is comparing the two roots this method is MEANT to have, one per panel, not a finished root against a half-written one. Unlike the Avocado caveat above, the CPU move carries NO precision term here: CANDI's evaluation runs under `no_autocast`, so no bf16 path is exercised on either device and the pass is fp32 on CPU exactly as it would have been on a MIG slice (slurm/t81_predict_candi.sh's own header, and src/candi/bench/dump.py:241). The checkpoint behind both panels is the V_-selected best.ckpt — epoch 14, chosen on V_ imputation macro CRPS under the uniform §5 rule with early stopping at epoch 20, md5 26aeefc87534006dd987d480a1963935, architecture read from the run json t81_eic_19_s0.json. The store-truth V_breadth rows stamped 2026-09-04 were scored off that V_cpu root by job 58031933 at --mem=128G --cpus-per-task=33, a resubmission raised after the 32 G original 57953580 died OUT_OF_MEMORY 9 h in; the raised job COMPLETED 0:0 and is the sole writer of the store.V_.json those rows read. Cited to cruxvault/results/t81/TRAIN_CANDI_EIC19.md, sections "CPU-sharded relaunch (2026-09-03, K16)", "eic_19 B_ shard repair (2026-09-03)" and "Score-pass OOMs and resubmissions (2026-09-03)", and §12.6.

eic.pilot.label: eic.pilot→20,21,22
eic.pilot.subtitle: trained on the ENCODE Pilot Regions
eic.pilot.rows_note: The same ten methods as eic.19. The naive baselines are fit once and their one number is printed in both regimes, because their fit does not depend on the training loci.
eic.pilot.eli5: The ablation. Same model, same eval chromosomes, a different training slice of similar size — the 44 ENCODE Pilot Regions, minus their overlap with chr20, chr21 and chr22. It asks whether the choice of slice moves the result. Avocado's own supplement claims it does not, and nobody has checked that for a sequence-conditioned model.

Under eic.pilot, Avocado's stage-1 fit returns to the ENCODE Pilot Regions and is faithful to its own paper for the first time (§3.2).
The training window count is a containment rule, not a division: the sampler plans 1,294 fully-contained 768-bin windows = 993,792 bins = 97.10 % of the contained budget.

Nothing on this board is ranked yet, and no gap between two rows is readable yet. Same as eic.19: §15's resolution limit (t86) is not measured, and AGENTS.md §7.2 records that a seed change alone moves pooled CRPS by 0.1195 while the target-clustered noise floor on macro CRPS is ~0.09.

ChromImpute's B_ rows are point-only on 3 of their 51 tracks, exactly as under eic.19: no ATAC-seq in the σ draw, so the three ATAC-seq B_ experiments carry no spread and the distributional metrics on those rows are aggregated over 48 tracks against 51 for the point metrics (`provenance.point_only_tracks`; cruxvault/results/t81/PRED_B_CI.md). Lavawizard's B_ rows carry the same gap on the same 3 tracks, for the same reason — ATAC-seq is not a training assay in its 12-cell σ draw either (cruxvault/results/t81/PRED_B_LAVA_PILOT.md §2.4, §7.7). Lavawizard's pilot σ table has a second, separate gap: it was fitted on 12 cells with 2 rare-mark self-pair tracks skipped, so H2AK9ac and H4K12ac have no σ row at all. Neither mark appears in this regime's V_ or B_ panel, so every row stamped here is unaffected by that second gap; a later panel carrying either would be point-only for it (cruxvault/results/t81/W3_LAVA_PILOT.md §S.7). avg-arcsinh's B_ rows on this board, under challenge truth and store truth alike, carry the same gap on the same 3 tracks again — it is scored against the eic.19 σ table, whose 29 assays do not include ATAC-seq — so their distributional metrics are over 48 of their 51 tracks as well (cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_B.md). Avocado's B_ rows on this board carry the same gap on the same 3 tracks again, for a third variant of the same cause: its pilot σ table skips no track and holds 31 assays over 98 tracks, but ATAC-seq is not one of those 31, so the three ATAC-seq B_ experiments read `sigma_source` `none` under store truth and challenge truth alike and their distributional metrics stand over 48 of their 51 tracks against 51 for the point metrics. Read from `provenance.point_only_tracks` in each B_ json and from the table at /project/def-maxwl/mforooz/t81_sigma/Avocado/sigma_eic_pilot.json; Avocado's V_ rows here are unaffected, with `sigma_source` `sigma_table` on all 45 scored V_ tracks (cruxvault/results/t81/W3_AVOCADO.md). eDICE's B_ rows on this board carry the same gap on the same 3 tracks again: its pilot σ table skips no track and holds 31 assays over 98 tracks, but ATAC-seq is not one of those 31, so the three ATAC-seq B_ experiments read `sigma_source` `none` under store truth and challenge truth alike, and the distributional metrics on all three of its B_ rows — its two store-truth rows and the challenge-truth row stamped later the same day — stand over 48 of their 51 tracks against 51 for the point metrics. Its V_ rows here are unaffected, with `sigma_source` `sigma_table` on all 45 scored V_ tracks and `point_only_tracks` empty. Read from `provenance.point_only_tracks` in the B_ json and the table at /project/def-maxwl/mforooz/t81_sigma/eDICE/sigma_eic_pilot.json; cruxvault/results/t81/PRED_B_EDICE.md §2.

eDICE's σ table under this regime was fitted on chr1 and chr2 only, not on all 18 of the regime's training chromosomes: the full scope projected past the σ job's walltime band, and the launcher's own header prescribes narrowing with SIGMA_CHROMS rather than buying a wider one. The residuals are still cut to the Pilot Regions BED, and the row's `sigma_fitted_on` badge records the two chromosomes verbatim, so the narrowing is in the artefact and not only in a memo. It is a thinner fit than the eic.19 table's, and every σ-derived key on eDICE's rows here — crps, gaussian_nll, coverage_95, pit_ks — rests on it. Cited to cruxvault/results/t81/W3_EDICE_RERUN.md §5. That two-chromosome badge now stands over seven eDICE rows on this board rather than two: the V_breadth pair stamped 2026-09-02, the store-truth B_ and V_matched rows stamped 2026-09-03, held-out and genome-wide each, and the challenge-truth B_ row stamped the same day. The `sigma_fitted_on` string is byte-identical on all seven, so the thin fit reaches the test panel as well as the selection panel, and it reaches the second truth as well as the first — and on the three B_ rows it reaches only 48 of their 51 tracks, for the ATAC-seq reason the point-only caveat above records.

The genome-wide column here is the same partial field as on eic.19: §4 blanks it for Avocado, ChromImpute and Lavawizard, so eDICE, CANDI and the naive baselines are the methods that can have one. CANDI is position-generalizing — it pins no parameter to a genomic position — so a genome-wide cell is legitimate for it, and it now has one: its store-truth V_breadth cell stamped 2026-09-04. Its challenge-truth B_ pass scored the held-out chromosomes only, so at THAT address its genome-wide number is still NOT COMPUTED rather than withheld. Fourteen are stamped so far: eDICE's V_breadth cell and its store-truth B_ and V_matched cells, avg-arcsinh's V_breadth, V_matched and store-truth B_ cells, knn1's store-truth V_breadth, V_matched and B_ cells, avg's and knn5's store-truth V_breadth cells, knn5's store-truth B_ and V_matched cells stamped 2026-09-04, and CANDI's store-truth V_breadth cell stamped the same day. It is never ranked.

knn1's challenge-truth B_ row on this board carries no distributional cell on the pval arm at all. The pass ran with no σ table and knn1 keeps a single contributor, so it has no cross-cell spread: `provenance.sigma_source` reads `none` on all 51 of its tracks and the scorer withheld every σ-derived key. `pval/crps`, `pval/pit_ks`, `pval/coverage_95` and `pval/gaussian_nll` are ABSENT from the row rather than zero, and its badge is the third σ state, `point-only — no spread`. Its point metrics stand over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays as every other row at this address, so those columns are directly comparable and only the distributional ones are blank. This is the same absence knn1's eic.19 rows carry, measured again on this board's own score json rather than carried over from them. Read from the row's own `missing_metrics` and the score json's `provenance.sigma_source`; cited to cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_B.md. The same four keys are ABSENT for the same reason from its two store-truth B_ rows stamped 2026-09-03, held-out and genome-wide: that pass ran with no σ table either, `provenance.sigma_source` reads `none` on all 51 tracks of its score json and `point_only_tracks` names all 51, each row records the four in its `missing_metrics` and that is the whole of each list, and each was stamped with --allow-missing only after the gate refused it by name. Their point columns stand over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays as every other row at each of those addresses, so only the distributional pval cells are blank there too. On the count arm those two rows are the exception rather than the rule: knn1 carries one over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays while Avocado, ChromImpute, Lavawizard, avg-arcsinh and eDICE all read 0 experiments there. It no longer stands alone: knn5's two store-truth B_ rows, stamped 2026-09-04 off its own eic_pilot prediction root rather than a collapsed one, carry a count arm over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays, so each B_ count sub-board here now holds two methods rather than knn1 by itself — a departure from the standing knn1 still holds at store.B_ on eic.19. The same four keys are ABSENT for the same reason from its four store-truth V_ rows stamped 2026-09-03 — V_breadth and V_matched, held-out and genome-wide — which were all stamped off the one store.V_ score json: that pass ran with no σ table either, its `provenance.sigma_source` reads `none` on all 45 of its scored tracks and its `point_only_tracks` names all 45. Each of the four rows records those four keys in its `missing_metrics` and that is the whole of each list, and each was stamped with --allow-missing only after the gate refused it by name. Their point columns stand over the same 45 experiments and 22 assays on V_breadth, and the same 21 and 7 on V_matched, as every other row at each of those addresses, so only the distributional pval cells are blank there too. On the count arm those four rows carry one where most rows do not: knn1 carries a count arm at every store-truth address on this board — 45 experiments over 22 assays on both V_breadth rows and 21 over 7 on both V_matched rows. It no longer stands alone at every one of them: avg's store-truth V_breadth rows stamped 2026-09-03, held-out and genome-wide, carry a count arm over the same 45 experiments and 22 assays, and knn5's two, stamped the same day off its OWN eic_pilot prediction root rather than a collapsed one, carry one over the same 45 and 22, and CANDI's own two stamped 2026-09-04 carry one over the same 45 and 22 again, so each V_breadth count sub-board here holds four methods. At store.V_matched and at both store.B_ addresses knn1 no longer stands alone either: knn5's store-truth V_matched and B_ rows, stamped 2026-09-04, carry a count arm over the same 21 experiments and 7 assays and the same 51 and 8, so each of those four count sub-boards now holds two methods; every remaining row at them still reads 0 experiments. Nothing at any of those addresses is ranked, so that too is a coverage fact and not a placement.

marginal's row on this board carries no `pval/gwcorr` and no `pval/gwspear`. The baseline predicts one constant value per track, so its prediction has zero variance and its Pearson and Spearman correlation against the truth is undefined — not a number, per track, by construction: a property of the baseline and not a failed pass. Under this board's rule an undefined metric on a baseline is DROPPED with this caveat, never silently and never as 0: the scorer wrote neither key into `macro.pval` nor into `panels.pval.B`, the row records both in `missing_metrics`, and the two correlation columns are blank for marginal alone. Every other key on the row is a real number over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays as the rest of the address, the distributional ones included: the constant track still carries its own per-bin `signal_sigma`, so the row's σ badge is `native heteroscedastic` and its crps, pit_ks, coverage_95 and gaussian_nll are computed rather than withheld. The scoring job's own `.err` records the two undefined correlations as warnings and exits 0. Read from the score json's own `macro.pval` key set and the row's `missing_metrics`; cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_B.md.

avg-arcsinh carries no count arm on any row on this board either, for the same reason it carries none on eic.19: the baseline takes the pval mean in arcsinh space and sinh's it back, so it predicts in -log10 p only, and the scorer wrote `macro.count` empty and every `panels[count]` block at 0 experiments and 0 assays. On its six store-truth rows — the two B_, and the two V_breadth and two V_matched rows stamped 2026-09-03 — the four count-arm registry metrics — `count/crps`, `count/crps_oracle_scaled`, `count/nb_nll` and `count/scale_error` — are ABSENT rather than zero, are recorded in `missing_metrics`, and are the whole of each list: no pval key is missing on any of them. Its challenge-truth B_ row records the same four for a different reason — under challenge truth the count arm is absent by rule for every method, which is also why that row alone adds `pval/auprc` and `pval/peak_base_rate` — so avg-arcsinh appears on no count sub-board here under either truth. Its pval columns stand over the same experiments and assays as every other row at the same address: 51 and 8 on the B_ rows, 45 and 22 on V_breadth, 21 and 7 on V_matched. Read from each row's own `missing_metrics` and the score json's own `macro` key set; cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_B.md.

Avocado carries no count arm on any row on this board either, for the same reason it carries none on eic.19: §7 gives no rival a count head, and the method predicts in -log10 p only, so the scorer wrote `macro.count` empty and every `panels[count]` block at 0 experiments and 0 assays. The four count-arm registry metrics — `count/crps`, `count/crps_oracle_scaled`, `count/nb_nll` and `count/scale_error` — are ABSENT from its V_breadth row rather than zero, are recorded in `missing_metrics`, and are the whole of that list: no pval key is missing. Its pval columns stand over the same 45 experiments and 22 assays as every other V_breadth row at this address, and the row was stamped with --allow-missing only after the gate refused it without. When that row was stamped, no row at store.V_breadth on this board carried a count arm, so that count sub-board was empty here rather than partial. That no longer holds: knn1's store-truth V_breadth rows stamped 2026-09-03, held-out and genome-wide, carry one over 45 experiments and 22 assays, and avg's two and knn5's two, stamped the same day, carry one over the same 45 and 22, and CANDI's two stamped 2026-09-04 carry one over the same 45 and 22 again, so each of those sub-boards now holds four methods rather than nobody. (The clause this replaced also called every row at that address a rival; avg-arcsinh's baseline row, stamped earlier, already made that half inexact.) Avocado's pilot σ table skips no track — 98 tracks over 31 assays, `skipped_tracks` empty — so the rare-mark gap recorded above for Lavawizard's pilot table does not reach it, and H2AK9ac and H4K12ac each have a σ row. Read from the row's own `missing_metrics`, the score json's own `macro` key set and the table at /project/def-maxwl/mforooz/t81_sigma/Avocado/sigma_eic_pilot.json; cruxvault/results/t81/W3_AVOCADO.md. The same four keys are ABSENT for the same reason from its store-truth B_ and V_matched rows stamped 2026-09-03, each stamped with --allow-missing only after the gate refused it by name, and their pval columns stand over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays (B_) and the same 21 and 7 (V_matched) as every other row at each of those addresses — where no other row carried a count arm when they were stamped. That no longer holds at either address: at store.B_ knn1's two store-truth rows stamped later the same day carry a count arm over 51 experiments and 8 assays, and at store.V_matched knn1's two store-truth rows stamped 2026-09-03 carry one over 21 experiments and 7 assays, so each of those two count sub-boards now holds two methods rather than nobody: knn1's two rows, and knn5's stamped 2026-09-04 over the same 51 experiments and 8 assays at store.B_ and the same 21 and 7 at store.V_matched. Nothing at either address is ranked, so that is a coverage fact and not a placement. Its challenge-truth B_ row records the same four for a different reason — under challenge truth the count arm is absent by rule for every method, which is also why that row alone adds pval/auprc and pval/peak_base_rate — and it needed no --allow-missing at all. The claim above that its pilot σ table skips no track is about the rare marks only and is not a claim that its rows carry no σ gap: the point-only caveat above records the 48-of-51 ATAC-seq gap on its B_ rows.

avg and avg-arcsinh are regime-independent baselines, so their rows on this board are the SAME measurement as their eic.19 rows rather than a second, independent one: both were generated once from the eic_19 generation root and scored at pilot addresses under plan/BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md §12.2 D1, a collapse licensed by the regime-independence assert of job 57804707 — each V_ manifest under /scratch/mforooz/t81_pred/<method>/eic_19/V_ carries `regime_independent` = {asserted_against: regime.eic_pilot.V_.json, chrom: chr20, identical: true}. Checked on the artefacts rather than carried over: every pval panel block of avg-arcsinh's V_ score json is bit-identical across the two boards (`panels.pval` sha256[:12] 2481740b2197 held-out and 2dab12745cf3 genome-wide), avg's challenge-truth B_ pval block likewise (f1b8719d9125), and avg's store-truth V_ score json likewise on both arms and both scopes (`panels.pval.V_breadth` sha256[:12] a78ec0a91ead held-out and fd2846a18ee7 genome-wide, `panels.count.V_breadth` 7d5decbf0f3e and 6bf22fd9e822, with `macro` and `per_track` equal too), each of those jsons names a pred_root under eic_19 while its own regime names eic_pilot, and avg-arcsinh's seven rows here carry a σ badge naming sigma.eic_19.json (avg fits no σ table at all and its badge is native heteroscedastic). So do not read the two boards' avg or avg-arcsinh cells as agreement between regimes, and never average them; cruxvault/results/t81/BASELINES.md §4 and §5, and cruxvault/results/t81/SCORES_BASELINES_B.md §1.2.

Avocado's V_ rows and its B_ rows on this board are not the same numerical path either, for the same reason they are not on eic.19. Its V_ predictions were made on a 1g.10gb MIG slice with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) live and its B_ predictions on CPU nodes in fp32 — predict.py:71 resolves the device to cpu when the allocation carries no GPU and predict.py:133 enables autocast only when device.type == "cuda" — because the GPU queue gave the once-only B_ arrays no projected start at all on 2026-09-03 and the pass was re-priced onto the CPU partitions. Nothing else differs: the same checkpoint, the same pilot σ table, the same sinh-and-clip inversion and the same declared panel, so the V_ to B_ step for Avocado alone carries an unmeasured precision term no other method's carries (cruxvault/results/t81/W3_AVOCADO.md §26).

CANDI's rows on this board were predicted on CPU nodes, not on a GPU, and the PI ruled on 2026-09-04 that those CPU roots ARE the canonical CANDI prediction roots. The V_ panel came from the 23-task chromosome-sharded array 57953585 (one chromosome per task, --gres=none --cpus-per-task=8 --mem=16G, all 23 COMPLETED 0:0) writing /scratch/mforooz/t81_pred/CANDI/eic_pilot/V_cpu, and that root is the ONLY CANDI V_ prediction root there is: no V_ directory exists beside it, the name V_cpu records the DEVICE the pass ran on and not a sibling status, and the GPU submission that would have written a V_ folder, 57944438, has never started — queued 2026-09-03T02:19, still PENDING (Priority) when these rows were stamped, and it has written nothing. The B_ panel is the canonical /project/def-maxwl/mforooz/t81_pred_B/CANDI/eic_pilot/B_, written by the 23-task array 57953588 of the same shape and merged into that single root by job 57983378. Both passes were re-priced onto the CPU partitions because the GPU queue gave the once-only CANDI predict jobs no projected start from 2026-09-02 19:25 onward. On the B_ array alone, task 0 (chr1) was killed OUT_OF_MEMORY against the 16 G ceiling — that array's own MaxRSS table puts chr2 at 15.99 G against the same ceiling and chr1 is 2.8 % longer again — so chr1 alone was re-predicted unsharded at 32 G (57983377) over the same root and merged with the other 22; the V_ array took no such kill and all 23 of its shards completed at 16 G. So a reader comparing a B_ cell here against a V_ cell is comparing the two roots this method is MEANT to have, one per panel, not a finished root against a half-written one. As on eic.19 the CPU move carries NO precision term, because CANDI's evaluation runs under `no_autocast` so no bf16 path is exercised on either device and the pass is fp32 on CPU exactly as it would have been on a MIG slice (slurm/t81_predict_candi.sh's own header, and src/candi/bench/dump.py:241). The checkpoint behind both panels is the V_-selected best.ckpt — epoch 5, chosen on V_ imputation macro CRPS on the count head over 45 scoreable experiments across full chr20-22 under the uniform §5 rule, md5 742f4251533b47e4c3ba34ef9ff53bd8 — and unlike eic_19's it was rebuilt from a RECONSTRUCTED architecture record: training job 57674899_1 was cancelled at its 16 h time limit before train.py writes the run json, so t81_eic_pilot_s0.arch.json carries the config.arch block copied verbatim from the probe run probe_eic_pilot_s0_3000 and proved by a strict load with no missing and no unexpected tensor (cruxvault/results/t81/PILOT_ARCH.md). The store-truth V_breadth rows stamped 2026-09-04 were scored off that V_cpu root by job 58031931 at --mem=128G --cpus-per-task=33, a resubmission raised after the 32 G original 57953587 died OUT_OF_MEMORY 7 h 54 m in; the raised job COMPLETED 0:0 and is the sole writer of the store.V_.json those rows read. Cited to cruxvault/results/t81/TRAIN_CANDI_EIC19.md, sections `CPU-sharded relaunch (2026-09-03, K16)`, `eic_pilot B_ shard repair (2026-09-03)` and `Score-pass OOMs and resubmissions (2026-09-03)`.
